text: so ok let me ask u how this is working. basically lets say i have a 4 sided plane. and so edges are 0 1 2 3, and so i click edge 3, and i extrude it. because this adds another 3 edges now, we get from edge 3, there is 4 5 6, now say i delete it. so from the way it sounds like, its going, even tho i deleted 4 5 6, they linger. and recreating another extrude anywhere, is going to try to take 4 5 6, but those are invalid now. what i dont understand tho is why are we acting like the id is sacred, if i delete it, and then i extrude again, the next one should be 7 8 9 with the other edge still 3, never try to regain deleted ids, just write new ones, and then when saving the model u can remove the ids that are invalid and then step back all the ids to clean it up. right? would that not just solve the problem
resolution: Traced the proposed monotonic-edge-ID theory against the live implementation and established that welded edge numbers are rebuilt cache indices, not persistent identities. The observed failure was instead a stale authored-part scope after undo; implemented scope rebasing and idempotent scope adoption so newly generated topology remains selectable without relying on reused or sacred edge numbers.
